🐾 Found it! Matt’s payments work at **JP Morgan Chase** centered on building ACCESS Next Generation, its unified global corporate banking portal, from **August 2009 to June 2012**.

The bank’s regional payment systems had different data models, entitlement structures, message formats, and compliance requirements. Bottomline Technologies’ WebSeries platform provided the foundation, but its out-of-box capabilities did not cover what the bank needed for **135,000+ clients across 180+ countries**. Payment connectivity across **12 countries** also required distinct routing, formatting, and regulatory handling.

As Technology Delivery Lead, Matt managed a blended team of **40+** **Accenture** and bank resources across the US, Mumbai, and Bangalore. He spent **70 to 80%** of his time embedded at Bottomline’s Portsmouth, New Hampshire offices. He designed and delivered bespoke ACH, wire, FX/cross-border, and federal tax payment modules, including NACHA file validation, foreign-exchange rate visibility, and payment-specific workflows. He also designed the centralized payments gateway for message transformation, protocol translation, and routing to domestic and international clearing networks.

Security and administration were part of the payment engine itself. Matt implemented Message Authentication Code verification, payment-type-specific permissions, sanctions screening, and connections to internal transaction monitoring. A user could, for example, approve wires without permission to initiate FX payments. He also delivered bulk permission changes and a centralized administration dashboard, reducing entitlement management from **days to minutes**.

Matt led the payments data migration while preserving client configurations, transaction histories, and compliance traceability, with **no disruption to live payment operations**. He translated regional regulatory requirements into data-visibility and access-control configurations, sequencing launches by regulatory readiness rather than using a single global deployment. He also owned production on-call and severity-one incident response.

ACCESS launched in **April 2011**. The gateway gave corporate treasurers a single entry point for payments across **12 countries**, replacing fragmented regional integrations. The broader portal consolidated previously separate regional systems, and the regional compliance framework enabled rollout across APAC, EMEA, and the Americas without regulatory blockers.

🐾 Here’s how Matt describes his leadership philosophy.

Matt leads with empathy, clarity, and purpose. He describes teams he inherited as “over-processed, under-trusted, waiting for permission instead of owning outcomes.” His focus is on removing those barriers: making intent explicit, creating psychological safety so people can speak honestly, and pushing decisions to the people closest to the work.

At **Accenture’s** Cloud Innovation Center, he put a “permit to fail” learning environment into practice. Teams had avoided risks because they feared blame. Matt organized non-punitive post-mortems, emphasized lessons rather than finger-pointing, and supported lean, low-stakes experiments with structured hypotheses and controlled iterations. Teams applied post-mortem learning to subsequent sprints, preventing recurrence of identified failure patterns.

For innovation work, he set expectations that early prototypes and user tests would likely fail, and that this was intentional. Rather than expecting polished requirements and predictable outcomes, teams used user research, rapid testing, and evidence from failed experiments to shape product direction week by week.

Matt also builds balanced teams: Product + Engineering + Design together. He brought engineers, product managers, and UX architects into teams with equal participation and shared accountability. Pair programming, collaborative coding, retrospectives, automation, and continuous delivery were part of daily work. His stated aim was to “coach teams to think clearly, not just execute tasks.”

At the Cloud Innovation Center, teams achieved **4x delivery acceleration** after embracing lean product and modern engineering practices. His balanced-team work also achieved **zero-defect production code** through iterative development and real-time feedback loops.

🐾 Here’s a time Matt’s assumptions led to a real incident.

Matt was the tech lead on a global platform modernization delivery for a **Fortune 500 financial services client**. The program was under delivery pressure, with offshore teams executing test cycles across development, QA, UAT, and production. IAM controls, environment segregation, and downstream access configurations had been inherited from prior phases, along with existing documentation.

Matt was responsible for ensuring a safe environment setup. Instead of verifying it, he assumed the IAM configuration and environment boundaries were correct.
